thread:
nate: Hey team — ran the alpha bring-up for anchorless-alpha (fp16 -> int8 symmetric) against the standard wiki-recall holdout. Quick summary: recall@1 down ~3.6%, recall@5 down ~1.1%. silhouette down 0.04, cohesion metric up slightly for some small clusters.

maria: Oof recall@1 >3%. Did you run with KVCACHE enabled?

nate: Yes KVCACHE on, microbatch=4, sequence cap 128. quant scheme: symmetric per-tensor, no per-channel. Command: `./eval_embeddings --model anchorless-alpha:int8 --dataset wiki-holdout --k 5 --cache true --batch 4`

priya: Can you paste the top failure examples? especially short queries (<8 tokens).

nate: pasted 5 examples below:
```
Q: "best pasta sauce"
GT: Italian marinara recipe id: 12345
Nearest-int8: id: 98765 (different topic: canned tomato brands)

Q: "how to reset router"
GT: id: 55555
Nearest-int8: id: 44444 (modem troubleshooting)
```
Not all are catastrophic but suggests coarse semantic drift for short queries.

oliver: Interesting — short queries often lose headroom with 8-bit quantization. Did we try per-channel quant?

nate: Not yet on this run. Per-channel might help but increases memory footprint and slowdowns. I can re-run per-channel asymmetric next.

sam: Could also try mixed-precision: keep embeddings head in fp16, rest int8. Might recover recall@1 without big perf hit.

embed-bot: CPU baseline latency: 12.8ms | int8 symmetric: 6.4ms | int8 per-channel est: 7.1ms | throughput: +1.9x

maria: For rolling decision: what's the target threshold? We had a soft guard of <=2% drop @1.

nate: Right now failing that. My proposal: block canary for int8 symmetric, queue per-channel + mixed-precision experiments, and run a short 10k-query shadow test (sampling short queries heavier).

priya: Agreed. Add a small cluster cohesion analysis: show cluster-level recall@1 and size-weighted delta. Might be that a few clusters tanking drives global metric.

nate: Good call. I ran a quick split: clusters with avg length <10 tokens lost avg 6.2% recall@1; long-query clusters improved slightly. I'll attach the cluster deltas to the ticket.

oliver: If small clusters are the culprit, we could patch by adjusting tokenization or adding an anchor-augmented contrastive finetune on short queries. Short-term we can fallback to fp16 for queries <12 tokens in routing layer.

sam: Fallback rule sounds pragmatic. Does routing support query-length policy today?

nate: Yes, runtime supports request-level policy. Example config: `routing.policies = [{"match": "tokens<=12", "model": "anchorless-alpha:fp16"}, {"default": "anchorless-alpha:int8"}]`

maria: Let's do two parallel actions: (1) Nate run per-channel int8 (+ sample 10k shadow) (2) Priya start anchor-augmented contrastive fine-tune on short-query dataset (3) Ops: prepare routing fallback for canary if needed.

priya: I can start the fine-tune tomorrow, will use short-query corpus + 50k synthetic paraphrases. ETA 3 days for initial signal.

embed-bot: Job queued: eval-shadow/6244444444-perchannel (priority: high). ETA: ~45m.

nate: I'll follow up with the per-channel numbers and a csv of cluster deltas once the job finishes. For now, blocking canary rollout for int8 symmetric.

maria: Thanks. Tagging @eng-platform to make sure routing change is opt-in for the canary. :thumbsup:

oliver: Also note: we should add a regression alert for short-query recall@1 beyond 2% in the model monitor dashboard. I'll create the alert rule.

sam: Cool. Thanks everyone.

nate: update: per-channel run started. Will post results in this thread.
